chunks.subject: AP Biology
chunks.title: Q6 — Analyze Data (4 points)
chunks.content: AP Biology Q6 (short FRQ, Analyze Data), 4 points, one per part. Context: the ald gene encodes ALD protein needed for correct chromosome alignment in meiosis; Figure 1A gives percent of metaphase cells with ALD-associated filaments and Figure 1B gives ALD protein amount for genotypes WT/WT, WT/del, ald1/del, ald3/ald23, ald23/del. A: identify the genotype with about 12% of metaphase cells showing ALD filaments (ald1/del). B: describe the difference in ALD protein production between ald3/ald23 and ald23/del (ald3/ald23 produces more; ald23/del produces less or none). C: use Figures 1A and 1B to support that cells can make a normal amount of filaments with about half the wild-type ALD protein (WT/del makes ~half the protein of WT/WT yet shows no difference in percent of cells with filaments). D: explain why WT/del and ald1/del differ in phenotype (Figure 1A) despite equal ALD protein amounts (Figure 1B) — WT/del has one allele making functional protein giving a wild-type phenotype, whereas the ald1 mutation yields reduced-function protein. Common failure: part C comparing the wrong genotypes; part D not addressing functional vs. reduced-function protein.

chunks.subject: AP Biology
chunks.title: Q6 exemplar — Sample 6A, 4/4
chunks.content: Q6 scored 4/4. A: ald1/del (~12%). B: ald3/ald23 produced less ALD than wild type but ald23/del produced none. C: WT/WT and WT/del have the same percent of metaphase cells with ALD filaments even though WT/del makes about half the ALD of WT/WT. D: the ald1 allele 'may produce a defective or otherwise malfunctioning version of the ALD protein, while the WT/del genotype produces at least one working copy.' Full-credit model contrasting functional vs. nonfunctional protein.

chunks.subject: AP Biology
chunks.title: Q6 exemplar — Sample 6B, 3/4
chunks.content: Q6 scored 3/4. Earned A (ald1/del ~12%), B (ald3/ald23 higher in ALD production), C (WT/del makes half the ALD of WT/WT yet the percent of metaphase cells shows no statistical difference). Lost D: did not explain why a protein mutation can change phenotype or which genotype it applies to. Shows a strong data-reading response that misses the functional-protein reasoning in part D.

chunks.subject: AP Biology
chunks.title: Q6 exemplar — Sample 6C, 2/4
chunks.content: Q6 scored 2/4. Earned A (ald1/del ~12%) and B (ald3/ald23 has more ALD protein). Lost C (compared the wrong genotype — used ald1/del instead of WT/del against WT/WT) and D (did not explain why WT/del and ald1/del differ in phenotype despite similar ALD amounts). Illustrates that misidentifying the comparison genotype breaks both the support (C) and explanation (D) points.
